<description>
**Problem:** AssumeUTXO verifies imported UTXOs against a hash we bake into the binary.
Every node reconstructs the same UTXO set during ordinary IBD, but [does not check its hash against the existing AssumeUTXO commitment](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/32377).

**Fix:** During ordinary block validation, verify the provided AssumeUTXO hash when block connection reaches the corresponding block, stopping the node on a mismatch.
Flush pending changes to disk before hashing the UTXO set and comparing the result with the commitment.

Keep only the latest AssumeUTXO commitment per network to limit the extra hashing work during IBD, and update the release process to replace it.
Users who need older snapshots for research or other purposes can use a compatible older release or restore the corresponding commitment as `m_assumeutxo_data` and recompile.
</description>

<new_statements>
[2026-10-24] c:6379792380 comment by ajtowns (member):
What's the performance impact when hitting such a block?

Doesn't this make the result of a release including bad snaphot data worse for everyone -- Alice who does IBD has her node crash despite having good data that she fully verified, and Bob who uses the bad snapshot still potentially fails to an incorrect chain unless Alice has already done her IBD run and Bob happens to hear Alice complain about the failure?

Having predictable snapshot points (every 14112 blocks [per bip452](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/pull/2137/files)) would allow every node to calculate the appropriate hash (in the background on a leveldb snapshot without cs_main held, hopefully) and remember it, prior to a new release being considered, making verification much easier, and consistent across implementations. Including the block's muhash in the assumeutxo set would also probably work here, since muhash is already calculated and stored in coinstatsindex.
</new_statements>
